tEn: How to Actually Make Launch Videos That Convert
tZh: 如何真正做出能转化的发布视频
sEn: Farza shares his playbook for making launch videos that actually convert, replacing big-budget premieres with constant mini demos on algorithmic platforms.
sZh: Farza 分享打造真正能转化的发布视频的方法论，用算法平台上的持续小样演示取代大预算的首发式。

consensus.en: Launching is not a one-time event but continuous demo shipping on algorithmic platforms.
consensus.zh: 发布不是一次性事件，而是在算法平台上持续发布演示。

consensus.en: Founders should work backwards from the demo: script, hook, and story before building.
consensus.zh: 创始人应从演示反向工作：在构建前先构思脚本、钩子和故事。

consensus.en: The hook and first 10 seconds are critical to stop scrollers and convey value.
consensus.zh: 钩子和前10秒对于阻止滚动和传达价值至关重要。

consensus.en: Show your process, not just the polished end result; authenticity resonates.
consensus.zh: 展示你的过程，而不仅仅是精美的最终结果；真实性会引起共鸣。

consensus.en: Every channel has different conversion rates; track and optimize for actual signups.
consensus.zh: 每个渠道的转化率不同；跟踪并优化实际注册。

consensus.en: Audio quality is the most important production element; invest in a good mic.
consensus.zh: 音频质量是最重要的制作元素；投资一个好的麦克风。

contrarian.en: Don't spend time and money on a big fancy launch video; a simple iPhone video often performs better.
contrarian.zh: 不要花费时间和金钱制作大型精美的发布视频；简单的iPhone视频往往表现更好。

contrarian.en: Posting frequently and accepting cringe is necessary to learn and improve.
contrarian.zh: 频繁发布并接受尴尬是学习和改进的必要条件。

contrarian.en: Don't obsess over views; focus on retention and actual user engagement.
contrarian.zh: 不要痴迷于浏览量；关注留存和实际用户参与度。

contrarian.en: Twitter has low conversion despite high views; YouTube and Instagram convert better.
contrarian.zh: Twitter尽管浏览量高但转化率低；YouTube和Instagram转化更好。

contrarian.en: You don't need expensive production; a phone and laptop make you powerful.
contrarian.zh: 你不需要昂贵的制作；一部手机和笔记本电脑就能让你强大。

contrarian.en: Targeted small views (e.g., 4,000) can be more valuable than viral views for lead generation.
contrarian.zh: 有针对性的小浏览量（例如4,000）对于潜在客户生成可能比病毒式浏览量更有价值。

turns.en: These days, too many founders think launching is all about spending a ton of time and money to produce a slick video and hoping it hits. But my guest today, Farza Majeed, has a totally different approach to launching and going viral.
turns.zh: 如今，太多创始人认为发布就是花大量时间和金钱制作一个精美的视频，然后希望它能火。但今天我的嘉宾 Farza Majeed 对发布和走红有着完全不同的方法。

turns.en: He's the founder of Hey Clicky, where his posts regularly get millions of views.
turns.zh: 他是 Hey Clicky 的创始人，他的帖子经常获得数百万次浏览。

turns.en: And today, he's going to share his playbook for how to create videos that actually convert.

turns.zh: 我甚至会读第一句话吗？因为如果我不读第一句话，我根本不可能深入进去。另外，看看视频的第一帧。它非常刻意地是 Xcode。为什么？因为我知道最初好奇的开发者可能会对此感兴趣。而不是真正的视频编辑，对吧？所以，它刻意是 Xcode。我刻意放大到这里这个部分来展示，因为这个部分太小了。这个部分就像这个小三角形，帮你一下。大多数人在滚动时只看到前 3 秒。

turns.en: Everyone. So, this is click.
turns.zh: 每个人都是。所以，这是点击。

turns.en: Zoom. And I go, "Oh, what is that?" You know, at least while you're scrolling.
turns.zh: 放大。然后我说：“哦，那是什么？”你知道，至少在你滚动的时候。

turns.en: Yeah, and you're moving it around so people can see that there's something moving there.
turns.zh: 是的，你把它移来移去，这样人们就能看到那里有东西在动。

turns.en: I think that, um, you can go into details all day, but the reason I got this I know this stuff now is because there's hundreds and thousands of videos I've made that nobody has cared about. Yeah. I think that's the biggest thing. Like, yeah, I don't want people to watch this video and think, "Oh, I got to make this hook and do this and this."
turns.zh: 我认为，嗯，你可以整天深入细节，但我现在知道这些东西的原因是因为我制作了成百上千个没人关心的视频。是的。我认为这是最重要的事情。就像，是的，我不希望人们看了这个视频然后想：“哦，我得做这个钩子，做这个那个。”

turns.en: And so, this was this first one off the cuff. This was almost entirely unplanned. And so, a lot of this was just you and instinct and how you put this together based on things you've learned. Walk us through another video that that maybe you planned out a little bit more in advance cuz one thing that's surprising to me, you actually write a script for all of your videos and I think anybody that's seen one of your videos would be surprised by that because you seem like you're just talking off the cuff. How do you do that? Like you you're very prepared but it doesn't seem formal and stuffy and like you're reading. How can you teach somebody else to do that?
turns.zh: 所以，这是第一个即兴的。这几乎完全没计划。所以，很多只是你的直觉和你基于学到的东西如何组合起来。带我们看另一个视频，也许你提前计划得更多一些，因为让我惊讶的一件事是，你实际上为你所有的视频都写脚本，我想任何看过你视频的人都会对此感到惊讶，因为你看起来就像在即兴说话。你是怎么做到的？你准备得很充分，但看起来并不正式、呆板，也不像在念稿。你怎么教别人做到这一点？

turns.en: Totally. If I like reading it, then that means it'll probably sound good if I say it out loud as well.
turns.zh: 完全正确。如果我喜欢读它，那意味着我大声说出来可能也会好听。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But not always but sometimes. And so this is one example of a script I wrote for a video that I did yesterday. And again, it's just super simple like do I enjoy reading this? Like would I read this if I just someone texted this to me?
turns.zh: 但不总是，但有时是。所以这是我昨天做的一个视频的脚本例子。再说一次，它超级简单，就像我喜欢读这个吗？如果有人把这个发短信给我，我会读吗？

turns.en: Yeah, what's going through your head? Are you imagining the audience listening to this or how do you evaluate if something is actually good and interesting?
turns.zh: 是的，你脑子里在想什么？你是在想象观众听这个，还是你如何评估某件事是否真的有趣和好？

turns.en: For me, it's always I'm the audience.
turns.zh: 对我来说，永远是我就是观众。

turns.en: Would I be interested in what the script is saying?
turns.zh: 我会对脚本的内容感兴趣吗？

turns.en: Honestly, this script is actually not that strong, but I still recorded the video because you've got to be launching. In the first little bit, am I getting across what I'm doing? Why is it important? You can get across so much in just 10 seconds. What you're doing, why it's important—let's get into it. That's what the first 10 seconds of any kind of video should be about, because most of these videos are 1-minute long, right? It's kind of a movie. A movie is an hour and a half, 2 hours, and the first 20 minutes is just a setup.
turns.zh: 说实话，这个脚本其实没那么强，但我还是录了视频，因为你得发布。在开头一点点，我有没有传达出我在做什么？为什么重要？你可以在短短 10 秒内传达很多信息。你在做什么，为什么重要——让我们进入正题。这就是任何视频前 10 秒应该讲的内容，因为这些视频大多只有 1 分钟长，对吧？它有点像电影。一部电影是一个半小时、两个小时，前 20 分钟只是铺垫。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: It's a 2-hour thing. And so for a video that's 1-minute long, you need a setup but it should only be like 10, 20%. So I write this down and so in this case, I said, "Hi, I want to share a new demo of our new agent interface." When talking to our users, blah blah blah, and then getting into the demo. And so for me, this is just kind of how I think through it before I get in front of the camera. The worst part is being in front of the camera and you're like, "Ah, what am I saying?" You have nothing to ground yourself.
turns.zh: 它是一个两小时的东西。所以对于 1 分钟长的视频，你需要铺垫，但应该只占 10%、20%。所以我写下来，在这个案例中，我说：“嗨，我想分享我们新智能体界面的新演示。”当与用户交谈时，等等等等，然后进入演示。所以对我来说，这就是我在镜头前思考的方式。最糟糕的部分是在镜头前，你会想：“啊，我在说什么？”你没有什么可以支撑自己的。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It's good to ground yourself, yeah.
turns.zh: 让自己有支撑是好的，是的。

turns.en: You start with the script and then you move on to some of the visuals. How do you think about what that first shot should be? It's so important, right? It's the first thing people see when they're scrolling.
turns.zh: 你从脚本开始，然后转向一些视觉元素。你如何考虑第一个镜头应该是什么？这非常重要，对吧？这是人们滚动时看到的第一件事。

turns.en: I'll show you a quick example of one of our videos. So this video actually did really good on YouTube. This is like a brand new fresh YouTube channel. We literally made it and then posted this video 3 days later.
turns.zh: 我快速给你看一个我们视频的例子。这个视频在 YouTube 上其实表现很好。这是一个全新的 YouTube 频道。我们 literally 创建了它，然后 3 天后发布了这个视频。

turns.en: Yep.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And this is one of our highest converting videos, despite being 19,000 views. Yeah, this video, I think it did like 3 million views on Twitter,
turns.zh: 这是我们转化率最高的视频之一，尽管只有 19,000 次观看。是的，这个视频，我想它在 Twitter 上获得了 300 万次观看，

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: 20,000 on YouTube, and like some crazy amount on Instagram as well. The same video. So, it kind of did it across—we posted just everywhere, just to see what happens. But yeah, I mean, the way I like to do my videos is: who is the person making this thing? Just show yourself. Show your face very clearly. This is you. This is your personality. Just be proud of who you are, and confidently tell the camera what you're working on. Because if you think it's cool, then I think you'll find at least—my thought is always at least one other person will think this is cool.
turns.zh: YouTube 上 20,000 次，Instagram 上也有疯狂的数量。同一个视频。所以它有点跨平台——我们到处发布，只是看看会发生什么。但是的，我的意思是，我喜欢做视频的方式是：制作这个东西的人是谁？就展示你自己。非常清晰地展示你的脸。这就是你。这是你的个性。为自己感到骄傲，自信地告诉镜头你在做什么。因为如果你觉得这很酷，那么我想你会发现至少——我的想法总是至少还有一个人会觉得这很酷。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And that's who I'm talking to. I'm talking to that one other person in that world that may think this is cool. And so, yeah, I always start with a very clear "Hi, this is what I'm working on."
turns.zh: 这就是我在对话的人。我在和那个世界上可能觉得这很酷的另一个人对话。所以，是的，我总是以一个非常清晰的“嗨，这就是我在做的事情”开始。

turns.en: All you got to do is press and hold at 10 plus control, start talking, and whatever you're saying will stream in as text into whatever text box your cursor is on. For example, if I'm on Apple Notes, I can just say—
turns.zh: 你只需要按住 10 加控制键，开始说话，你说的任何内容都会以文本形式流式传输到你光标所在的任何文本框中。例如，如果我在 Apple Notes 上，我可以直接说——

turns.zh: 太好了，就是这样工作的。你能给我一个例子吗？

turns.en: Hey, today I have to ship three things. First, skills, second, memory, and third, this bug that this one user gave about dictation.
turns.zh: 嘿，今天我要发布三件事。第一，技能，第二，记忆，第三，这个用户给出的关于听写的 bug。

turns.en: Okay, that's pretty cool, but this is like every other product I've ever seen. There's nothing special about this.
turns.zh: 好的，那很酷，但这就像我见过的所有其他产品一样。这没什么特别的。

turns.en: So, that's pretty cool, and honestly, many products already do this exact thing today. But here's the thing: when I'm writing, I often don't really know what I even want to say. So, check this out. We're shipping—
turns.zh: 所以，那很酷，说实话，今天很多产品已经做到了这一点。但问题是：当我写作时，我 often 并不真正知道我想说什么。所以，看看这个。我们正在发布——

turns.en: So, then like, I frame the problem for myself.
turns.zh: 那么，然后就像，我为自己框定问题。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: I'm not saying "Everyone has this problem where they don't know what to write." I'm not involving everybody. I'm only talking about myself. And because these are my problems, because I'm always building stuff for myself.
turns.zh: 我不是说“每个人都有这个问题，他们不知道写什么。”我没有涉及所有人。我只谈论我自己。因为这些是我的问题，因为我总是为自己构建东西。

turns.en: Screen away dictation. It's pretty cool. I've never seen anything like it before, and I want to show you. Let's say I want to write—
turns.zh: 屏幕外听写。这很酷。我以前从未见过这样的东西，我想给你看。假设我想写——

turns.en: Again, that's just me being myself, which is like, "Hey, I want to show you."
turns.zh: 再次，那只是我做自己，就像，“嘿，我想给你看。”

turns.en: You come across very natural here. Was that easy for you to do that in the beginning?
turns.zh: 你在这里显得非常自然。一开始对你来说容易做到吗？

turns.en: First of all, this whole video is scripted. Every line that I'm saying, I wrote like 3 days before. And I said it and I will say it in my head like over and over and over again, in the shower, going to work, and I'm always like, "How should I say that line?" And by the time I'm in front of the camera, I've already visualized it like 10 times. And it's so funny, after this video we finished it, I told Vikrant, the person who I make videos with, and I'm like, this is the worst video we've ever done. It's not even worth editing it. And he's like, no, bro, be quiet, shut up. I'm going to make it and then we're going to post it. And so again, it's good to have the team also be really like, hey, we made this, we're going to put it out. It doesn't matter how cringe we think it is, we'll let the audience decide. This video did 3 million views on Twitter. And people went crazy over it. And it's so funny, I thought it was horrible. I just thought like, this is so bad. So this is one of the situations where I was wrong. And I think founders, I mean, me especially, think something we made is bad, or I made is bad, and then I don't want to put it out because it's going to make—I don't like how it sounds or feels, I'm constantly forcing myself to put it out. It's not natural for me to click post. But sometimes it is. Sometimes it's not. Yeah. And so this is one example where I was like so surprised that people even cared to begin with, because I thought it was just a pretty simple thing.
turns.zh: 首先，整个视频都是脚本化的。我说的每一行，我都是大约 3 天前写的。我说了，我会在脑子里一遍又一遍地说，在洗澡时，上班路上，我总是想：“我该怎么说出那句台词？”等到我站在镜头前时，我已经在脑海中想象了 10 次。有趣的是，这个视频完成后，我告诉 Vikrant，和我一起制作视频的人，我说，这是我们做过的最差的视频。甚至不值得编辑。他说，不，兄弟，安静，闭嘴。我要制作它，然后我们要发布它。所以再次，有团队也很好，他们会说，嘿，我们做了这个，我们要发布它。不管我们觉得它有多尴尬，我们让观众决定。这个视频在 Twitter 上获得了 300 万次观看。人们为之疯狂。有趣的是，我觉得它很糟糕。我只是觉得，这太糟糕了。所以这是我说错的情况之一。我认为创始人，尤其是像我这样的，认为我们做的东西不好，或者我做的东西不好，然后我不想发布，因为这会让我——我不喜欢它的声音或感觉，我不断强迫自己发布。点击发布对我来说并不自然。但有时是。有时不是。是的。所以这是一个例子，我很惊讶人们甚至关心，因为我认为这只是一个非常简单的事情。

turns.en: It's interesting, I've heard you talk about this almost like demo-driven development where everything that you're working on, you're almost working backwards from a demo that you want at the end of it. And that's kind of the proof that the thing is ready to go, it lets you test it out, and then you get to the end of it and you're like, let's just publish the demo.
turns.zh: 这很有趣，我听说你几乎把这称为演示驱动开发，你所做的一切，几乎都是从你最终想要的演示倒推。这有点像是证明东西已经准备好了，让你测试它，然后你到了最后，你会说，我们就发布演示吧。

turns.en: The most important thing in my company that I try to always—and every company I've ever run—is, you know that feeling when you're working with someone, often on the team or a co-founder, and you're like, yo, check this out. You have to be so aware of that, because that is the thing that you could probably talk about online. That check this out is exactly like that raw check this out, is exactly how you should be kind of presenting yourself on the internet. In this case, sometimes I go a little bit more fancy if I want to, but sometimes I'm also just a guy in a simple video, and in the YC office. And then sometimes, maybe once a quarter, we'll do a polished launch, where it's like, this is something I'm really proud of, I want to make sure it's talked about properly.
turns.zh: 在我的公司里，我试图始终做到的最重要的事情——以及我经营过的每家公司——是，你知道那种感觉，当你和某人一起工作，通常是团队或联合创始人，你会说，哟，看看这个。你必须非常意识到这一点，因为那可能就是你可以在网上谈论的东西。那个“看看这个”正是那种原始的“看看这个”，正是你在互联网上展示自己的方式。在这种情况下，有时我会更花哨一点，如果我想的话，但有时我也只是一个在简单视频中的人，在 YC 办公室。然后有时，也许每季度一次，我们会做一个精心制作的发布，就像，这是我真正引以为豪的东西，我想确保它被正确地谈论。

turns.en: But generally, we're launching like demos every single day almost. It's interesting, now that everybody can put out videos and do launches every single day, how do you stand out in that world? It seems like people that are spending lots of money and trying to do fancy produced videos, that's an effort to try to get more attention and stand out and seem polished and further along than you are. But you take the opposite approach. And so in a world where there's just so much content and so many videos that are out there every single day, how do you think about how you try to stand out and how others can, too?
turns.zh: 但一般来说，我们几乎每天都在发布演示。有意思的是，现在每个人都能发视频、每天发布，你怎么在那个世界里脱颖而出？看起来那些花很多钱、做精美视频的人，是在努力获取更多关注、显得更精致、比你走得更远。但你采取了相反的做法。所以在一个每天都有那么多内容和视频的世界里，你怎么考虑脱颖而出，以及其他人怎么也能做到？

turns.en: I never think about like that. I always just think about like I'm I want to talk about something. I think it's interesting. And there's got to be one person out there that thinks it's interesting.
turns.zh: 我从来不那样想。我总是只想：我想聊点什么。我觉得它有意思。外面总会有一个人觉得它有意思。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And when I click post, in my brain, I'm always like if this gets zero attention, zero views, I'm still happy I posted it. You know, because I'm glad I got something out there. I think that should be the mentality everybody has working on their company launching 2026. Like you can't be thinking about it. By the time I hit post, I've already forgotten it. I'm looking at it maybe a week later.
turns.zh: 当我点击发布时，我脑子里总是想：如果这得到零关注、零观看，我仍然高兴我发布了它。你知道，因为我高兴我把东西发出去了。我认为这应该是每个在 2026 年做公司发布的人的心态。你不能老想着它。等我按下发布，我已经忘了它。我可能一周后才看。

turns.en: Yeah. How do you do that? I feel like most people when they post something they're incessantly just refreshing and trying to see are people liking it, who liked it. But you launch and you walk away.
turns.zh: 是啊。你怎么做到的？我觉得大多数人发东西时会不停地刷新，想看有没有人喜欢、谁喜欢了。但你发布完就走开了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: How do you get to that point?
turns.zh: 你怎么达到那个境界的？

turns.en: I mean, you just put so much garbage out there. I put so much garbage out in the world at this point. Not like bad stuff, but just like stuff that I wasn't like this is I didn't think that I didn't think was good.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，你就是把很多垃圾发出去。我现在往世界上发了太多垃圾。不是坏东西，只是那些我当时不觉得好的东西。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.zh: 而且人们第二天就忘了。我现在可以做点东西发出去，人们第二天就忘了。2026 年的注意力差不多就是这样运作的，你懂吗？

turns.en: And so this is like a perfect example. This is 2021. Mhm. It's a year after YC. I'm like a I'm a solo founder. I've been a solo founder at ZipSchool and a solo founder at Buildspace, solo founder now. It's not like I'm that Yes, I know how to put a camera in front of me and edit it, but I'm not a fantastic editor. turns.en: Hey there, ZipSchoolers. Faraz from ZipSchool here again to show off four new classes that we just added yesterday to ZipSchool that we are very excited about. The first one is called Mars Perseverance Rover Landing aimed at kids ages 7 to 12. And this class covers the Mars landing that actually Honestly, it is not I'm already checked out watching this video.
turns.zh: 嘿，ZipSchool 的各位。我是 ZipSchool 的 Faraz，又来展示我们昨天刚加到 ZipSchool 的四门新课程，我们非常兴奋。第一门叫“火星毅力号着陆”，面向 7 到 12 岁的孩子。这门课涵盖火星着陆，其实——老实说，不是——我看这个视频已经走神了。

turns.zh: 你会怎么做不同？你在这个视频里犯了哪些错误？

turns.zh: 我认为那才是重要的部分。关键不在那个。关键在于我发布了它，然后它得到了 23 个赞，顺便说一句，这比零多。它得到了不止零次观看。它得到了不止零条评论。它得到了一个人的一条评论。

turns.en: You got a bookmark.
turns.zh: 你得到了一个书签。

turns.en: I got a bookmark. So like I launched. This to me is a launch. And I know that sounds dumb to maybe some, but to me this is exactly what launching means. We did something new at the company. We talk about it to the into the world and it doesn't matter if we got 23 views. If there's a chance that we get more than one view, we should talk about it. And so this is a super small thing. This is like an everyday thing in my company where we have cuz we have new classes dropping everyday almost. And so I just make it I'd be like, yeah, let's talk about it. Maybe one day I'll talk about it and one of the classes will be really interesting and get picked up and go super viral, which never happened. But the fact is I made the videos. And over time I I got so much better at just knowing like how should I talk about products? turns.zh: 我觉得另一个独特之处是，你实际上在早期团队上投入了很多，团队很小，但很大一部分是为了帮助你创作、制作并定期把这些视频发布出去。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean I always say like I'm okay at videos. There are people out there who are way better than me.
turns.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我总是说我在视频方面还行。外面有很多人比我强得多。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: My first two hires were—I knew from the beginning, even before I started my company, it's going to be number one, a filmmaker, and number two, an engineer. And this number one is filmmaker for me. So that is the first one. Or whatever order they can come in.
turns.zh: 我的前两个员工是——我从一开始就知道，甚至在我开始创业之前，第一个是电影制作人，第二个是工程师。对我来说，第一个就是电影制作人。所以那是第一个。或者他们能进来的任何顺序。

turns.en: Why was that so important to you?
turns.zh: 为什么这对你如此重要？

turns.en: I don't want to put a ton of attention every day on making videos. I mean any founder watching, any founder in YC, like nobody wants to do that every day. At some level you do have to in the beginning in the early days. And yeah, I mean look at my Clicky videos, like I'm forcing myself to just make videos and make stuff every day. At one point, you're like, well, this would be really great if someone's full-time job at my company was to kind of observe what we were doing and help us launch and constantly make it their mission to make us look good when we launch as well and make us come off properly. And so that's why a filmmaker was one of the first hires I made at this company. And at my last company, our film team was two people. We were only like a seven-person team.
turns.zh: 我不想每天把大量注意力放在制作视频上。我的意思是，任何在看这个的创始人，任何 YC 的创始人，没人想每天都做那个。在某种程度上，在早期你确实必须做。是的，看看我的 Clicky 视频，我强迫自己每天只是做视频和做东西。到了某个时候，你会想，好吧，如果我公司里有人全职工作就是观察我们在做什么，帮助我们发布，并不断把让我们在发布时看起来好看、让我们表现得体作为他们的使命，那就太好了。所以这就是为什么电影制作人是我在这家公司最早雇佣的人之一。在我上一家公司，我们的电影团队是两个人。我们当时只有七个人的团队。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So even at this company, at one point at Clicky, we had three people making videos and one engineer. It's so funny now, it's so easy to pump out more code and more software, but it's harder than ever to actually talk about what you are doing in a coherent way in front of an audience.
turns.zh: 所以即使在这家公司，在 Clicky 的某个时候，我们有三个人做视频，一个工程师。现在很有趣，产出更多代码和软件太容易了，但要在观众面前以连贯的方式谈论你在做什么，却比以往任何时候都难。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Because now, Aaron, you know, someone can clone my product in like two minutes at this point. But again, what's really hard to clone is the audience and the community that I built around what I'm doing and the energy around it. If you got an audience around your company, I'll say 100,000 people that was really into what you were doing, maybe enterprise AI, you know, maybe something around like photography or whatever, whatever your niche is,
turns.zh: 因为现在，Aaron，你知道，有人可以在两分钟内克隆我的产品。但再次，真正难以克隆的是我围绕我所做的事情建立的观众和社区，以及围绕它的能量。如果你的公司周围有观众，我说的是 10 万人真正热衷于你正在做的事情，也许是企业 AI，你知道，也许是摄影之类的，无论你的细分领域是什么，

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: that'd be useful. Because that's why, you know, I can make a video now about a new feature and like thousands of people flood my app. That's awesome. That's like every founder's dream, right?
turns.zh: 那会很有用。因为这就是为什么，你知道，我现在可以做一个关于新功能的视频，然后成千上万的人涌入我的应用。那太棒了。那就像每个创始人的梦想，对吧？

turns.en: Tell us more about the gear that you're using today to produce these videos.
turns.zh: 跟我们多讲讲你今天用来制作这些视频的设备。

turns.en: Yeah, so for demos on my computer, which is just like what I'm hacking on that day, I always use this thing called Screen Studio. I think it's made by some indie hacker. It's just really good. It records your screen, records your local audio, makes your cursor look good, and I think it costs like 30 bucks. That's like one level. Then the next level is like, well, videos that more include me in a more kind of native way, and for that I just pull up my iPhone. Literally just a selfie camera and just record myself talking, post, or edit on my phone even. I use on my phone—it's Instagram's editing tool, it's called Edits, a lot. So when I do edit on my phone a good amount. So that's the iPhone. Nothing else required. But then there's like the next level where it's like you feel like you want to do something a little bit more thought through, cinematic, and that's where I use my Sony FX3. Sony FX3 or Sony FX3? The cheaper one. Along with a DJI mic. It's actually funny, the most important— This is actually so important. I can't believe I missed this. The most important thing in any video you make doesn't matter if it's a shitty Loom or a shitty little video or your iPhone is audio quality. If your audio is bad, I'm bouncing. I've watched some demos that are like 720p and just like the guy's in like a weird room in a basement, but his audio is crisp. And what he's working on is actually genuinely interesting, so I stick around. And so I don't care about the rest of it. I don't care what he looks like, anything. I'm like, I can hear him and I can see what he's doing. That's it. Yeah. And so I think if every founder could just invest in one of the super cheap DJI mics, find them used online, or just any mic that's not your MacBook mic, your or your AirPod mics, those don't count, that would be really good. And then for editing on my actual laptop I use DaVinci. Yeah. And maybe the most important part of my stack—he's not here right now, but Vikrant. Vikrant has made all the Hey Clicky videos. And without that guy making me look good and making us look good, none of this would happen. And so I don't want to sit here and be like I made all videos and did all this stuff. Every video we just looked at, apart from the Bad Zip School ones which were made by me, are made by Vikrant. And so, having a person that is actually talented at filmmaking, storytelling, writing next to you is like the biggest bonus a founder could have today.
turns.zh: 是的，所以对于我电脑上的演示，也就是我那天在捣鼓的东西，我总是用这个叫 Screen Studio 的东西。我觉得它是由某个独立黑客制作的。它真的很好。它录制你的屏幕，录制你的本地音频，让你的光标看起来好看，我想它大概 30 美元。那是一个级别。然后下一个级别是，视频更多地以更自然的方式包括我，为此我就拿起我的 iPhone。真的就是自拍相机，录下自己说话，发布，甚至直接在手机上编辑。我在手机上用 Instagram 的编辑工具，叫 Edits，用得很多。所以我在手机上编辑相当多。那就是 iPhone。不需要其他东西。但然后还有下一个级别，你觉得你想做一些更有思考、更有电影感的东西，那就是我用索尼 FX3 的时候。索尼 FX3 还是索尼 FX3？便宜的那个。加上一个 DJI 麦克风。实际上很有趣，最重要的——这实际上太重要了。我简直不敢相信我错过了这个。你制作的任何视频中最重要的东西，不管是一个糟糕的 Loom 还是一个糟糕的小视频还是你的 iPhone，是音频质量。如果你的音频不好，我就走了。我看过一些演示，像是 720p，就像那家伙在一个奇怪的地下室房间里，但他的音频很清晰。而他正在做的事情实际上真的很有趣，所以我留下来。所以我不在乎其他的。我不在乎他长什么样，什么都不在乎。我就想，我能听到他，我能看到他在做什么。就这样。是的。所以我认为如果每个创始人都能投资一个超级便宜的 DJI 麦克风，在网上找二手的，或者任何不是你的 MacBook 麦克风、你的 AirPods 麦克风的麦克风，那些不算，那就真的很好。然后在我实际笔记本电脑上编辑，我用 DaVinci。是的。也许我技术栈中最重要的部分——他现在不在这里，但 Vikrant。Vikrant 制作了所有 Hey Clicky 的视频。没有那个人让我看起来好看，让我们看起来好看，这一切都不会发生。所以我不想坐在这里说所有视频都是我做的，所有事情都是我做的。我们刚刚看的每个视频，除了 Bad Zip School 的那些是我做的，都是由 Vikrant 制作的。所以，身边有一个真正有电影制作、讲故事、写作天赋的人，是当今创始人能拥有的最大 bonus。

turns.en: So, a big part of how I work with Vikrant, who's the person who helps me with all these videos, is we just brainstorm. We're like, "Hey, we made this feature. What should— How should we make the video now? What are we thinking? Where should we do it?" And so, Vikrant is actually the main guy that's like, "Hmm, I had this shot idea." Or, "Hmm, I had this hook idea." Or, "Hey, I have this other idea." And often I'm the guy that's bringing the script and the song and the vibe that I'm going for. Because as the founder, I think you'll slowly find what are the things that you're good at in video making. There's some aspect to it. So, for me, I find I'm really good at writing and I'm really good at the music. And then Vikrant is good at literally everything else. From shooting to picking the set to editing after to, you know, all the little motion graphics he does. Just so talented. And then as the founder, me as Farza, I can go back to focusing on growth, hiring, making the product.
turns.zh: 所以，我和 Vikrant 合作的一大部分——他是帮助我制作所有这些视频的人——就是我们只是头脑风暴。我们会说：“嘿，我们做了这个功能。我们应该——我们现在应该怎么做视频？我们在想什么？我们应该在哪里做？”所以，Vikrant 实际上是那个主要的人，他会说：“嗯，我有这个镜头想法。”或者，“嗯，我有这个钩子想法。”或者，“嘿，我有另一个想法。”而通常我是那个带来脚本、歌曲和我想要的氛围的人。因为作为创始人，我想你会慢慢发现你在视频制作中擅长什么。它有一些方面。所以，对我来说，我发现我很擅长写作，我很擅长音乐。然后 Vikrant 擅长其他一切。从拍摄到选择场景到后期编辑，你知道，他做的所有小动态图形。太有才华了。然后作为创始人，我作为 Farza，我可以回去专注于增长、招聘、做产品。

turns.en: I don't want to spend all my time on making videos, you know? I don't think any founder watching this wants to do that. And look, I think a lot of people watching probably can't afford to hire a filmmaker or an actual person on their team. They're maybe just solo or they're co-founders. And what I'll say is, hey, go back to my old Zip School videos. Go back to—just scroll through any of my social media and look at all my old shitty videos and just start somewhere. That's the most important thing about making launch videos and launching today: you got to start. And the more you keep doing it every day, the more natural it'll become, and slowly, hopefully, more people check out your product. Hopefully you can then hire someone that does it even better than you.
turns.zh: 我不想把所有时间都花在制作视频上，你明白吗？我觉得任何看这个视频的创始人都不想那样做。而且你看，很多观众可能请不起电影制作人，或者团队里请不起专人。他们可能只是单打独斗，或者是联合创始人。我想说的是，嘿，回去看看我以前的 Zip School 视频。回去——随便翻翻我的社交媒体，看看我所有那些烂视频，然后就从某个地方开始。这就是制作发布视频和今天启动最重要的事情：你必须开始。你每天坚持做，它就会变得越来越自然，慢慢地，希望有更多人来看你的产品。希望到那时你能雇一个比你做得更好的人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So, for example, I'm not the engineer at my company anymore. I'm not the core engineer. I have someone that's a lot better than me.
turns.zh: 所以，举个例子，我不再是我公司的工程师了。我不是核心工程师。我有一个比我强得多的人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And same with filmmaking, same with design, same with every aspect of my company. But in the early days as a founder, you're doing everything.
turns.zh: 电影制作也一样，设计也一样，我公司的每个方面都一样。但在早期作为创始人，你什么都要做。

turns.en: It all.
turns.zh: 所有事。

turns.en: You're doing taxes, you're doing design, you're doing filmmaking. And so, you got to do everything. You can't be a little baby about it. You got to take out your camera and start posting some cringe stuff. Because in order to not be cringe, you must first be cringe, so yeah. And then yeah, for all of my writing, I always use this thing called Free Write. Um it's free to download, freewrite.io. It's my app. I built it actually just for this purpose.
turns.zh: 你要报税，你要做设计，你要拍视频。所以，你什么都要做。你不能像个小孩一样。你得拿出相机，开始发一些尴尬的东西。因为为了不尴尬，你必须先尴尬，所以是的。然后，是的，我所有的写作，我总是用这个叫 Free Write 的东西。嗯，它是免费下载的，freewrite.io。这是我的应用。我其实就是为了这个目的而构建的。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Uh yeah, free, open source, you can check it out. Maybe this is one thing I should—I didn't mention at all before—is writing is so important. So spend as much time as possible before the video writing it. So before you get in front of the camera and maybe record it, if you've never made a video, don't worry about this, but if you're like on your 15th, 20th, 30th video, try writing. Try writing for just 10 minutes about what it should be and then record it. Um you'll find that the more you think through it before you get to the video, the better it can possibly get. Because then you can catch a bad idea before it gets here.
turns.zh: 嗯，是的，免费、开源，你可以看看。也许这是我应该——我之前完全没提到——写作非常重要。所以在拍视频之前，尽可能多花时间写。所以在你站在镜头前，也许录制之前，如果你从未拍过视频，不用担心这个，但如果你已经拍到第 15、20、30 个视频了，试试写作。试着花 10 分钟写一下它应该是什么样，然后再录制。嗯，你会发现，在拍视频之前思考得越多，它就可能越好。因为这样你可以在坏主意出现之前就抓住它。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And that's it. That's my stack.
turns.zh: 就这样。这就是我的工具栈。

turns.en: I think you have a challenge for everybody who's watching for something they can do today to get started, right?
turns.zh: 我想你给每个观众都有一个挑战，让他们今天就能开始做点什么，对吧？

turns.en: My challenge to everyone watching this is: if you've never really made videos or if you have never really talked about your work online, but you've been hacking, you've been tinkering, you've been working on something—super simple. Every day, just spend 10 minutes, take your phone out, iPhone or Android, it's okay, and then just record yourself talking about what you were doing to what you did that day, and then post it to your social media of choice, Instagram, TikTok. You know what? Make a new Instagram account. So your existing followers don't even know. You do just post it somewhere. And do that for 30 days straight, and I promise you, within those 30 days, one of those videos will surpass probably 1,000 views. And then you can look back and ask yourself, hm, that one did 1,000 views. Maybe the next one, and you can learn from that, and you can make the next one based off the one that got 1,000 views. And you can slowly get better and better and better. That's the challenge, yeah. 30 days straight, every day one video. Send it to me. I'll be one of your likes if you're doing this challenge, and yeah, go for it.
turns.zh: 我对每个看这个视频的人的挑战是：如果你从未真正拍过视频，或者你从未真正在网上谈论过你的工作，但你一直在捣鼓、一直在折腾、一直在做点什么——超级简单。每天，只需花 10 分钟，拿出你的手机，iPhone 或安卓都行，然后录下你自己谈论你那天在做什么、做了什么，然后发到你选择的社交媒体上，Instagram、TikTok。你知道吗？注册一个新的 Instagram 账号。这样你现有的粉丝甚至都不知道。你就把它发到某个地方。连续做 30 天，我向你保证，在这 30 天内，其中一个视频的观看量可能会超过 1000。然后你可以回顾并问自己，嗯，那个视频有 1000 次观看。也许下一个，你可以从中学习，你可以基于那个获得 1000 次观看的视频制作下一个。你可以慢慢变得越来越好。这就是挑战，是的。连续 30 天，每天一个视频。发给我。如果你在做这个挑战，我会成为你的点赞之一，是的，去做吧。

turns.en: And it's never been easier to do this, right? To get that message out.
turns.zh: 而且做这件事从未如此容易，对吧？把那个信息传出去。

turns.en: It's never been easier. It's never been easier.
turns.zh: 从未如此容易。从未如此容易。

turns.en: Farza, thank you so much for being here. This is incredible advice.
turns.zh: Farza，非常感谢你来到这里。这是非常棒的建议。

turns.en: Anytime, man.
turns.zh: 随时，伙计。

tldr.en: Launching is continuous demo shipping on algorithmic platforms, not a one-time event.
tldr.zh: 发布不是一次性事件，而是在算法平台上持续交付演示。

tldr.en: Work backwards from the demo: script, hook, and story before building.
tldr.zh: 从演示倒推：先写脚本、钩子和故事，再动手开发。

tldr.en: Audio quality matters most; a good mic beats fancy production.
tldr.zh: 音频质量最重要；好麦克风胜过花哨制作。
